prompt:
An architect's presentation sheet for a small open-sided garden pavilion, drawn in fine black line work on warm white paper, showing two panels side by side with a printed caption under each.

The LEFT panel is captioned PLAN and is the pavilion seen from directly above. The RIGHT panel is captioned SOUTH ELEVATION and is the same pavilion's south front seen straight on from outside, from the south. Both panels are drawn to the same width, and the three things listed below must be plainly countable in BOTH panels.

The pavilion's south front has, and has nothing else:
- round columns standing in a row along the front, well apart from one another, drawn as small filled circles in the plan and as narrow uprights in the elevation;
- a front stair whose steps are drawn as separate parallel bars in the plan and as a stepped edge in the elevation;
- a front door in the plain back wall of the pavilion, drawn with a quarter-circle swing arc in the plan and as a tall rectangle in the elevation. There are no windows anywhere.

The two panels must agree on every one of these EXCEPT for exactly one deliberate discrepancy, which is the number of columns. Draw them like this:
- PLAN: 5 columns, 3 steps, 1 door.
- SOUTH ELEVATION: 6 columns, 3 steps, 1 door.
Nothing else may differ between the two panels: the step count and the door count must be identical in both, and no other feature may appear in one panel and be missing from the other. Every item is drawn clearly separated from its neighbours so it can be counted without doubt.

Clean architectural line work, no hatching, no dimensions, no text other than the two captions.
easy_question: This image was supposed to depict an architect's sheet with a PLAN panel and a SOUTH ELEVATION panel of the same small garden pavilion. A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram of the requested subject ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of the requested subject depicted, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.
